## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing. When the write fails, `save_report` discards the `OSError`, prints "Report saved to …" anyway, and returns 0, so a failed save looks like a successful one. This review read both changed files in full and traced the success and failure paths of `save_report` and `cleanup_report` against the added tests. These tests were read, not run. `cleanup_report` catches only `FileNotFoundError`, which matches its comment, and `test_cleanup_preserves_other_errors` checks that other errors still propagate.

## Changes
Adds `save_report`, which writes the rendered report to a path and prints where it went. Also adds `cleanup_report`, which deletes a temporary report and does nothing if the file is already gone, plus tests for both.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/reports.py:8 — silent-failure — Stop reporting success after a failed report write — If you call `save_report(tmp_path / "missing" / "report.txt")`, or use any destination where `write_text` raises `OSError` (missing directory, no permission, full disk), the function still prints "Report saved to <path>" and returns 0. The `except OSError: pass` at lines 8–9 swallows the error, and lines 10–11 then run as if the write succeeded. No log, comment or return value tells the caller that the fallback happened. — Users and calling scripts are told the report was saved when no file exists, so they lose the report without any sign of an error. — Fix: Let the `OSError` propagate, or return a non-zero code and print an actionable message to stderr naming the path and `strerror`. Only print the success line after `write_text` succeeds. Then rewrite `test_save_with_unavailable_destination` (tests/test_reports.py:46–47). It has no assertions and passes today even though the bug exists. It should assert either `pytest.raises(OSError)` or a non-zero return with no success message on stdout.
